name: Caílte

attributes.attribute: Fenian hero famed for fleetness of foot

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caílte is a Fenian hero, also written Cailte, Caoilte, Caelte, Keelta, and Kylta. Several bear the name, seven of them Fenians. Best known is Cailte mac Rónáin, sometimes a nephew of Fionn mac Cumhaill. Famous for fleetness of foot, he stewards for Fionn and catches wild animals in pairs for Gráinne. He kills giants and recites tales with a golden tongue. In Acallam na Senórach he lives into Christian times, speaking the old values to Patrick. Imram Brain has him reveal Fionn as the reborn King Mongán. Later ballads prefer Oisín. Barrán is his father-in-law, Suain his daughter. Scottish lore calls him Derglas, Macpherson's Ossian Co-alt. Some read Caílte and Oisín as nicknames for Fionn.

okr.objective: Caílte is the swift Fenian survivor who carries the old tales into Christian Ireland.
key_results: Several figures bear the name, and seven of them are Fenians.
The best known is Cailte mac Rónáin, sometimes a nephew of Fionn mac Cumhaill.
He wins fame for fleetness of foot and serves as steward for Fionn.
He catches a breeding pair of every wild creature at the ask of Gráinne.
He speaks for the old values to Patrick in Acallam na Senórach.
In Imram Brain he discloses that Fionn was reincarnated as King Mongán.
Later ballads largely displace him with Oisín.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. 'Caílte'
